record.paper_title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N
record.original_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs. For a sequence z_n → p ∈ ∂Ω and a base point z_0 ∈ Ω, define the sequential horosphere E_{z_0}({z_n},R) = {z ∈ Ω : limsup_{n→∞}[k_Ω(z,z_n) − k_Ω(z_0,z_n)] < (1/2) log R}. Is it true that Ω has the Denjoy–Wolff property exactly when the closure of every sequential horosphere meets the boundary ∂Ω in only one point?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.8. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Assume ∂Ω does not contain non-trivial analytic discs. Then Ω has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of any sequential horosphere touches ∂Ω at just one point.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ be a bounded convex domain, and assume that the boundary $\partial\Omega$ contains no non-trivial analytic discs (i.e., there is no non-constant holomorphic map $\varphi : \mathbb{D} \to \partial\Omega$ from the unit disc $\mathbb{D} \subset \mathbb{C}$). Let $k_\Omega$ denote the Kobayashi distance on $\Omega$. Fix a base point $z_0 \in \Omega$, a sequence $\{z_n\} \subset \Omega$ converging to a boundary point $p \in \partial\Omega$, and a real number $R > 0$. Define the sequential horosphere
$$E_{z_0}(\{z_n\}, R) := \Big\{ z \in \Omega : \limsup_{n\to\infty}\big[k_\Omega(z, z_n) - k_\Omega(z_0, z_n)\big] < \tfrac{1}{2}\log R \Big\}.$$
Say that $\Omega$ has the Denjoy–Wolff property if for every holomorphic self-map $f : \Omega \to \Omega$ with no fixed point in $\Omega$, there exists $\xi \in \partial\Omega$ such that the iterates $f^n$ converge to the constant map $\xi$, uniformly on compact subsets of $\Omega$.

Prove or disprove: $\Omega$ has the Denjoy–Wolff property if and only if, for every choice of $z_0 \in \Omega$, every sequence $\{z_n\} \subset \Omega$ converging to a point of $\partial\Omega$, and every $R > 0$, the closure $\overline{E_{z_0}(\{z_n\}, R)}$ in $\overline{\Omega}$ intersects $\partial\Omega$ in exactly one point.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a recent conjecture about a characterization of the Denjoy–Wolff property in terms of sequential horospheres for bounded convex domains in $\mathbb{C}^N$ whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs. One direction (the "if" implication) is known, and a recent example produces a smoothly bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$ without analytic discs in the boundary that fails the Denjoy–Wolff property. No source verifies the full equivalence, and the conjecture appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: On the failure of the Denjoy-Wolff theorem in convex domains
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a bounded convex domain in C^2 with C^∞-smooth boundary, containing no non-trivial analytic discs, that does not have the Denjoy-Wolff property.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist showing one cannot drop hypotheses, but they do not resolve the conjectured horosphere characterization.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in C^N
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: a bounded convex domain (without analytic discs in the boundary) has the Denjoy-Wolff property iff closures of sequential horospheres touch the boundary at a single point.
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence is stated as a conjecture; one implication is known.
